summary: Tennessee lost 27-24 at South Carolina after a late turnaround. Penalties and possession security lead the corrections; the Vols have an open date before Kentucky’s November 7 visit.

items.headline: Tennessee loses 27-24 on a last-second field goal
items.tldr: South Carolina tied the game late and won after a strip sack. Keep the final-possession lesson tied to ball security and field position.
items.outlet: Associated Press via Laredo Morning Times

items.headline: Penalties erase three potential touchdown passes
items.tldr: Rocky Top Insider details scores nullified by flags. Watch pre-snap alignment and blocking discipline before treating the passing stat line as the whole offensive story.

items.headline: Bishop runs 32 times for 120 yards and a touchdown
items.tldr: The running back helped Tennessee recover from an early deficit. Watch the next availability update after RTI reported that he was hurt late; a return timeline is not established.

items.headline: Tennessee records five second-half sacks
items.tldr: Pressure helped the defense work back into the game. The next test is to close the quarterback’s escape lane and finish the late scoring possession.

items.headline: Kentucky visits November 7 at 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
items.tldr: Both teams have an open date first. The confirmed homecoming window gives fans an evening at Neyland to plan around.

lead.headline: Keep the points you earn.
lead.body: Get aligned before the snap and keep the block legal through the throw. Secure the football when pressure arrives, while the defense finishes pursuit instead of letting the quarterback turn contact into a score.

matchup.thesis: Make the whole scoring play count
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Pair the first read with disciplined protection. A completed touchdown only helps when the formation, timing and blocks all survive the same down.

signals.title: Penalty discipline
signals.summary: Set the formation before the snap
signals.detail: Watch shifts, alignment and the line’s path through the play. Keep the offense from giving back the space its route design creates.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with penalty discipline?

signals.title: Late-possession security
signals.detail: Keep the receiving outlet available and the ball protected when the pocket narrows. End the down deliberately before contact decides the next field position.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with late-possession security?

signals.title: Running-back workload
signals.detail: Separate the last game’s production from the next game’s clearance. Watch confirmed personnel before deciding how the carries should be distributed.

signals.title: Defensive pursuit
signals.detail: Bring the pass rush with a clear edge and a second tackler. Finish through the quarterback’s hips rather than allowing the first missed contact to extend the drive.
